item.title: Five local Ministers set to travel abroad for St. Patricks Day
item.description: More than a third of the Cabinet will travel to the United States for St Patrick's Day in a diplomatic offensive aimed at the American establishment. Taoiseach Micheál Martin will visit Washington DC and Philadelphia while Ministers will also travel to Boston, New York, Atlanta, Savannah, Chicago, Austin and San Francisco. item.title: Management at Mullingar Hospital advising public to consider all health options
item.description: Management of the Midland Regional Hospital in Mullingar are advising the public to consider all health options. That's after an increasing in numbers of people requiring admission at this time. Where possible, patients with non-emergency conditions are being advised to seek assistance from other parts of the health service such as their local Pharmacist, GP, or a GP out of hours service. item.title: Investigation continuing into a theft from a house in Longford
item.description: An investigation is continuing into a theft from a house in Longford. The incident happened in the early hours of Friday, January 23rd in the St. Michael's Road area of the town. A sum of cash and some items of jewellery were taken during the course of the incident. No arrests have been made. Anyone with any information is asked to contact Longford Garda Station. item.title: Roscommon Cllr says Government needs to progress plans for Athlone
item.description: A South Roscommon Councillor says the Government need to progress plans to turn Athlone into Ireland's first Green City. Fianna Fáil's John Keogh was speaking after developer Sean Mulryan presented his plans for the midlands town at yesterday's council meeting. Ballymore hope to turn Athlone into a green city by 2040 but say the Government now need to fully back the plan. Cllr Keogh says action needs to be taken now to ensure the project progresses: Advertisement

item.title: Edgeworthstown man jailed for 13 years for raping elderly, vulnerable neighbour
item.description: An Edgeworthstown man who attacked and raped his elderly, vulnerable neighbour during a violent home invasion, causing her “life-altering” harm, has been jailed for 13 years. 36-year-old Shane Kelly forced his way into the 70-year-old woman's home late at night and subjected her to an ordeal in which he forced himself on her sexually, choked her and robbed her of petty cash, the Central Criminal Court heard. item.title: Calls for staged payments to housing scheme
item.description: A local councillor has called for the introduction of staged payments to increase applications for a Government housing scheme. The Croí Cónaithe Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant Scheme was first introduced in 2022. It's paid in arrears following the completion of work to bring vacant properties back into residential use. item.title: Minister: St Patrick's Day visits are not a 'jolly' for Government reps
item.description: A local Minister says foreign visits as part of St Patrick's Day events are not jollies for Government representatives. Minister of State Frank Feighan was speaking after it was confirmed that 50 cities around the world would be visited this year. item.title: Lough Funshinagh residents 'in limbo' ahead of Dublin meeting
item.description: Residents near the flood-affected Lough Funshinagh in Roscommon say they've been left in limbo due to a delay in securing a long-term solution. A planning application for a permanent pipeline was due to be submitted last year but was delayed.
